transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doc. Thanks for fitting me in. I, uh, I hope I'm not taking up time from people who are really sick, but... well, I guess what finally got me in here is just that I've been a little, I don't know, scattered lately? 

Over the last few months, my mind just keeps jumping around. Like, I'll be in the truck, and every little CB chirp, or a fuel price sign, or just some new idea popping into my head, and my attention is just pulled right to it. It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I take a lot of pride in my route and I normally never miss things. But I've been letting little details slip. You know, missing a client’s delivery note, or forgetting who I promised to call back. 

It's nothing too terrible, I swear, just... not like me. Does that make sense? I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in to talk about it.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood along with these attention problems—like feeling unusually high, irritable, or down?

Well, I guess... maybe a little bit? I don't want to make a big deal out of it, because I know everyone has their good and bad days, right? But, um, for the last few months, I have been feeling a bit... fired up, I guess you could say. Like, really optimistic, feeling like everything is just going to work out perfectly, no matter what. Which is a good thing, mostly, right? 

But then... well, I have to admit, and I feel bad even saying this, but I've also been getting a little snappy at home. Just over silly little things in the yard or around the house. It's not really like me to lose my patience like that. I try to be a good guy, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a jerk. I just... I don't know, my mood has just been kind of running a little hot and cold lately. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?

Have there been specific times when your mood felt distinctly elevated or high, like you were on top of the world, or unusually irritable, where it was clear to you or others that you were acting differently than usual?

Yeah, I guess... I guess that's exactly what I was trying to say, sorry if I was rambling a bit before. But yeah, for months now, it’s really been just like that. I’ll be either way too fired up, just convinced everything is going to work out perfectly no matter what, or... well, or I’m snapping over really small stuff at home and out in the yard. 

And that really isn’t my usual way at all. My wife has definitely given me a look a few times when I've lost my temper over a garden hose or something silly, so I know it's obvious to her, too. I feel terrible even admitting it, honestly, because I just want to be an easy guy to be around, you know? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. Does that... does that help answer your question, Doc?
Can you think of a specific time when this fired-up or snappy mood was really noticeable, maybe lasting a whole day or more, where you felt like you weren’t quite yourself?

Well, I mean, I guess it's been pretty much a daily thing, honestly. Like I was saying, for months now I've just been in this... this state where I'm either way too fired up, just so sure that every little thing is going to go my way, or I'm just getting short with people over nothing. 

Like the other day, I was trying to fix a sprinkler head in the yard, and it wouldn't thread right, and I just... I threw the wrench across the lawn. And that's just so not me, Doc. I'm usually the kind of guy who just takes a breath and tries again. I felt awful about it as soon as I did it, especially since my neighbor was outside. I just... I hope you don't think I'm an angry person or anything, because I really try not to be. It's just been going on like this for a while now. Is that... is that the kind of specific thing you meant?

When you say this has been happening for months, have there been times when these mood changes lasted for several days in a row, where you felt like you weren’t yourself at all—even if things came back to normal after a while?

Well, yeah, it's... it's actually been pretty much every day. Not just a few days in a row and then back to normal. It's really been going on like this for about seven months now. 

That was right around the time my daughter moved back home with us. Which is great, you know, I love having her there. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about my own kid, because I'm happy to help her out. I've just been trying so hard to keep everything steady and provide a good environment, and... I guess I've just been stuck in this mode ever since. Just running hot and cold, day after day, trying to keep the ship upright. 

I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than I should, or making it sound like I'm blaming her, because I'm definitely not. I'm just trying to be a good dad. Does that make sense, Doc? Is that the kind of timeline you were asking about?
Have there been times when your mood was so high or intense that it felt different from your usual self, like you were on a different level emotionally, even if it didn’t last very long?

Well, um, I know you asked about it maybe not lasting long, but like I was trying to say earlier... it's really been this way for months. I just... I'm either way too fired up, you know, just feeling like absolutely everything is going to work out perfectly no matter what happens... or I'm getting snappy over just tiny little things around the house and out in the yard. 

And I know I keep repeating myself, I'm sorry, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. It's just that being that fired up or that irritable... it really isn't my usual way at all. I've always tried to be an easygoing guy, so feeling this way for so long is... well, it's just not me. I really hope I'm explaining this okay, Doc. Is that what you were looking for?

Have you had any distinct periods where you felt unusually energetic, unusually confident, or driven to achieve goals — like your mind was racing or you had so much energy you didn’t need much sleep — even if it didn’t last very long?

Well... I guess I have been feeling pretty driven lately, yeah. I just keep finding extra jobs for myself to do. Like, I'll be rewriting my route plans for work to make them more efficient, or... or I'll be calling to check on the new drivers after hours, just to make sure they're settling in okay. I really hope my boss doesn't think I'm overstepping or anything, because I'm honestly just trying to be a good team player, you know? 

And then at home, I'm constantly finding things to fix around the house. It's just... if I sit still for too long, I get this really antsy feeling. I feel like I just have to be doing something useful. I mean, working hard and staying busy, that's usually a good thing, right? I hope I'm not making it sound like a bad thing... I'm just trying to give you the best answer I can. Is that the kind of energy you were asking about, Doc?
Can you describe a time when your mood was so high or so irritable that it was clearly different from your usual self, even if just for a few hours or part of a day?

Gosh, I'm sorry, Doc, I know you keep asking about these shorter times, and I really want to give you a good example... but I honestly just can't think of a time where it was just for a few hours or a part of a day. 

It's not like I have these big, crazy spikes or outbursts or anything like that. I'd never want to act out of line, especially around my daughter or the guys at work. Like I was trying to say before, it's just been this steady sort of... overdrive for the last several months. I haven't really had a moment where I felt completely out of control or totally different just for an afternoon. 

I really hope I'm not being difficult by not having a specific day or a few hours to tell you about. I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so you can do your job. Does that help at all, or am I completely missing what you're asking me?

Have you had a period of at least several days in a row where your mood was so high, irritable, or intense that it was clearly different from your usual self—like you were on a different level emotionally or acting out of character?

Well, um... no, not really just for a few days, either. I know you're trying to pin down a specific time frame, and I really want to give you one, I do. But like I was saying, it's just been this... this constant hum for months now. 

I haven't had any sort of dramatic shift where I was acting totally out of character for a week and then went back to normal. I'm still me, you know? I'm still showing up for work, still taking care of my family. It's just that I've been running a little hotter, I guess, for a long stretch now. 

I really hope I'm not frustrating you, Doc. I know you have a checklist of things you need to ask, and I feel bad that I keep giving you the same answer. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Have you ever had a period, even just a day or two, where you felt unusually upbeat, energized, or irritable—like you were in overdrive—where others might have noticed a change in you, even if it didn’t last very long?

I... I'm so sorry, Doc, I feel like I'm just a broken record here. I really don't mean to be difficult, I promise. But... no, I haven't had anything like that for just a day or two, either. 

It's just been this same, steady push for the last few months. I haven't had any sudden spikes where I'm suddenly acting totally different or... or snapping at people and then going back to normal. I'm just trying to keep up with everything and do a good job. I really hope I'm not wasting your time by not having a better example for you. Am I... am I answering this okay? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.

Have you had a time when your mood was clearly different from your usual self—like you were unusually high, overly confident, or extremely irritable—where this lasted for at least four or more days in a row?

Well... I know I keep saying it's been going on for months, and I guess that does mean it's lasted for at least four days, right? I'm sorry, I should have just said yes to that part earlier. I didn't mean to make this harder for you.

But, um, yeah... for the last few months, I guess I have been a little different. It's not bad, really! It's just... I've been feeling really fired up, you know? Like everything is just going to work out perfectly, no matter what. I guess you could say I've been pretty confident. 

And... well, I guess there have been times where I've been a little more irritable than usual, too. Not at work, of course! But maybe snapping a little over small things around the house or out in the yard. It's not really like me to do that, and I always feel terrible about it after. I'm usually a pretty easygoing guy. 

I hope that answers your question a little better? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this all out. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?
Can you confirm if there was a time when your mood was clearly different from your usual self—like you were unusually high, overly confident, or extremely irritable—for at least four days in a row?

Yes, doc, I can definitely confirm that. I'm sorry if I didn't make that clear enough just a second ago, I really don't want to make your job harder. 

But yes, for months now, it's been exactly like that. I've just been... well, either way too fired up, feeling like everything is going to work out no matter what, or... on the flip side, I'm snapping over just small, silly stuff at home and out in the yard. Which really isn't my usual way, I promise. I'm normally a pretty calm guy, so I hate that I've been doing that. 

Does that help clear it up for your notes? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need so we can get this figured out.
